newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
LALOO YADAV MEETS GOVERNOR, SAYS CBI MISLED GOVERNOR

Bihar state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav on Wednesday accused the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) of "cheating and hoodwinking" state governor A.R. Kidwai in obtaining sanction for Yadav's prosecution in the fodder scandal. At his meeting with the governor, Yadav demanded the governor ask the CBI to get clearance from the attorney-general before prosecuting him and others in the scandal. Yadav said the governor had assured him that he would look into the matter.
The Hindustan Times
OPPONENT DEMANDS LALOO YADAV'S RESIGNATION

The Janata Dal party's working president Sharad Yadav on Wednesday advised Laloo Yadav, his main rival for the party's presidentship, to quit as Bihar state's chief minister. Sharad Yadav gave the advice after consulting former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary Harkishen Singh Surjeet. The Marxist leader said that since the governor gave permission to prosecute Laloo Yadav, the issue was threatening the credentials of the ruling United Front.
The Economic Times
RESERVE BANK TIGHTENS NORMS FOR NON-BANKING FINANCE FIRMS

The Reserve Bank of India on Wednesday announced a two-phased, five percentage point increase in the statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) requirements of non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). This is the first change in NBFC guidelines after the CRB Capital Market fiasco. The RBI said NBFCs would have to increase their investment in gilts by 2.5 percentage points by January 1, 1998, and another 2.5 percentage points by April 1, 1998. This means they will have to maintain SLRs of 12.5 percent and 15 percent. The bank on May 2 lowered the average SLR requirement of NBFCs by 250 basis points from 12.5 percent to 10 percent.
RPG GROUP SELLS 11 PCT SULZER SHAREHOLDING

The RP Goenka (RPG) group has sold 11 percent of its holding in Sulzer India to its foreign partner, Sulzer Corp of Switzerland. The Swiss firm now has a 51 percent stake while the RPG has only 29 percent. Earlier both had 40 percent stake each in Sulzer India, which produces machinery and engineering goods. The remaining 20 percent of the company's equity is held by the public. The Goenkas have sold their holding at 1,090 rupees per share, seven times higher than the price a few days earlier.
VOLUNTARY DISCLOSURE SCHEME LAUNCHED

The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) on Wednesday announced the launch of the Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme 1997 (VDS '97). The scheme offers those with undeclared incomes a last chance to declare them. It will be effective from July 1 to December 31. The CBDT chairman said the scheme would succeed. He said VDS '97 would get a good response as it was formulated and announced on requests from people from the parallel economy who were willing to be part of it. He said VDS '97 might be the last such offer from the government because the relaxed tax regime and changing economic growth pattern would make such schemes unnecessary.
Financial Express
NATIONAL BOURSE SOFTENS STAND ON MEMBERS' INDEMNITY BONDS

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) may free its members from furnishing indemnity bonds, provided they opt for compulsory pre-verification of all the deliveries they make at the exchange. It may also modify the terms of the indemnity bond to cover only those defaults which result from the introduction of bad papers into the system. The move follows representations by a section of NSE members. NSE authorities are believed to have favoured the suggestions and are likely to take such a decision.
BOMBAY BOURSE OUTLINES PROCEDURE TO DETECT FAKE SHARES

The Bombay Stock Exchange, expecting an increase in volumes with the introduction of on-line systems, has asked its members to beef up their risk management operations. This is because the exchange is anticipating an increase in risks involved in the form of fake, forged or stolen shares. It has recommended a procedure to help members prevent introduction of fake shares by clients and also help them in their dealings with the clients.
Business Standard
SENSITIVE INDEX TUMBLES FROM 52-WEEK HIGH

The 30-scrip sensitive index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) leapt to a new 52-week high on Wednesday after frenzied trading before tumbling at the close on a bout of profit-taking. The Sensex closed at 4,082.50, down 5.14 points over the previous close of 4,087.64, under acute selling pressure from local financial institutions. The markets lost ground towards the end of the trading session as the Unit Trust of India sold key counters.
AT KEARNEY TO START OPERATIONS IN INDIA

U.S.-based global management consultant firm AT Kearney Inc will launch its consultancy services in India in August as part of the firm's global growth strategy in 1997. It has already recruited 15 consultants for its Indian operations and is in talks with several Indian companies. Deregulation, delicensing and competition are opening up new avenues for the firm in India, said its managing director of Indian operations.
The Observer
NRI BOND ISSUE TAX DEDUCTION AT SOURCE MAY GO

The Finance Ministry is set to stop deducting tax at source from non-resident Indian (NRI) investment in bond issues of financial institutions. The move might give relief to institutions who were concerned about the lukewarm response of NRI investors to their bond issues. The step needs an amendment to the relevant section of the new Income Tax Act. The financial institutions feared the provision in the section would make NRI investment in bonds less attractive.
INDIA, SRI LANKA TO DISCUSS TRADE IMBALANCE

India and Sri Lanka are likely to discuss their trade balance, which Colombo says is extremely unfavourable. Commerce Ministry officials said representatives of the two countries were likely to meet in June to discuss the Sri Lankan list of 84 items on which Colombo seeks bilateral tariff concessions. The list was first presented in April this year, but at that time there was only a caretaker government in New Delhi and it requested that talks be deferred. Another reason for the delay was that India had already announced its export import policy and could not incorporate new concessions.
